title: Ash on the Southern Road
text: By dusk, the fires along Ashbrook's southern wall had burned down to a low, sour smudge against the twilight. The surviving townsfolk did not cheer when the last of Vaelen's siege companies broke up the valley; they loaded handcarts in grim silence, wrapping cracked icons and sacks of damp seed-corn in wool blankets. Captain Garrick stood by the splintered gatehouse counting notched tallies on a wooden slate, each mark a neighbor left beneath the turnip fields outside the ditch. Behind the column, Thornwick's watchtowers already looked small and irrelevant, their signal beacons gutters of gray smoke in the drizzle. Ahead lay the Desiccated Marches—a cracked bowl of alkali flats, dry riverbeds, and fortified cistern-towns where water was weighed on apothecary scales and strangers were judged by the dust on their boots. Fenwick poled his flat-bottomed barge one final time across the border ford before burning the mooring ropes, watching the current carry charred timbers south toward the salt flats. Nobody spoke of victory around the first night's cookfires. Everyone knew Ashbrook had not been saved; it had merely been emptied in time.
cliffhanger: At midnight, scouts returning from the alkali rim reported that the wells of Redmarsh had been sealed from within—and someone was already marching north to meet the column.
unlocks_hint: Opens the Redmarsh caravan hub: water-rationing mechanics replace warmth, Tull and Zahra join as vendors and lore-brokers, and armored desert raiders replace border levies.

title: The Salt Wind Below
text: Ironheart Bastion did not fall with the roar of collapsing towers, but with the slow, metallic shriek of rusting sluice-wheels forced open after a generation of disuse. From the highest parapet of the forked peak, the victorious company looked down upon two very different worlds: behind them stretched the bleached ribs of Redmarsh, shimmering under a merciless white sun; ahead, beyond a jagged descent of switchbacks and wind-scoured scree, lay the gray-green haze of the Iron Coast. Quartermaster Bram spent the morning inventorying captured siege bolts and empty water barrels, muttering that the garrison had been defending ghosts and dried mud for years. Along the lower terraces, wounded mercenaries washed alkali grime from their faces in cold mountain condensation while Zahra copied faded hydraulic charts from the citadel's stone walls. The road down to Oakhaven was steep, narrow, and swept by salt gales that smelled of kelp, tar, and burning pine. For the first time in months, the boots of the army struck wet earth instead of cracked clay, though the distant boom of naval cannon across the bay warned that the sea offered no sanctuary.
cliffhanger: Before the vanguard even reached the coastal pines, black smoke began rising from the direction of Harborwatch—signals not of welcome, but of a fleet burning at anchor.
unlocks_hint: Unlocks Oakhaven port and coastal routes: naval artillery hazards, shipwright upgrades from Kors, healer triage contracts from Sera, and amphibious privateer enemies.

title: The Fleet Has Sailed. The Sword Remains.
text: The choking smoke over Harborwatch thinned beneath the cold wind off the Western Sea as Lord-Captain Korvus sank beneath the black surf with his twin anchors. Beyond the scorched seawall, the white sails of the evacuation armada—plated in black ironstone by Miner Gorin's freed smiths and caulked by the shipwrights pulled from the drowning tidal vaults—shrank into pinpricks against the slate-gray horizon, carrying Thornwick's survivors, Chief Healer Sera's wounded, seed-grain, and histories safely past the rim. The slipways lay utterly empty, only severed mooring ropes swaying in the black water. Standing beside Harbor Marshal Veyra, Bailiff Aldric, and the last bloodied veterans on the eastern pier, you turned your back to the quiet ocean. Fifty leagues inland to the east, the Obsidian Caldera had torn completely open in a pillar of white fire and shattered obsidian.
cliffhanger: Marshal Veyra wiped salt brine and black ash from her cutlass and stared toward the burning peaks: 'We have bought them their morning... now let us march into the night.'
unlocks_hint: Unlocks Highcrest Citadel: Tier 5 meteoric tempering from Weaponsmith Elda, pre-calamity truths from Archivist Orla, and the final reckoning in the Obsidian Caldera.

title: The Reckoning of Thornvael
text: In the silence beneath the sundered Infernal Sanctuary, the four-act tragedy of Thornvael reached its final balance—from Morvessa's Salt Tithe at the Border Fords and Gorrathul's dry cisterns atop Ironheart, to the burning piers of Harborwatch and the Threshold Chamber beneath the volcano. Highcrest Citadel fell quiet as Marshal Vance, Harbor Marshal Veyra, and Archivist Orla stood by the gate watching the horizon shift: whether cooled by the snapping of Arch-Warden Korrath's necrotic tether so the western sails might return to a fragile living morning, or sealed in obsidian glass beneath the blazing Crown of Thorns and Cinder claimed from Ember Overlord Vorak's kiln.
cliffhanger: Across four scarred provinces from Thornwick to the Obsidian Peaks, a new age dawned over a continent that had survived the end of the world.
unlocks_hint: Campaign Complete — Explore both Threshold endings (Crown of Order / Ember Reckoning) or challenge Nightmare & Hell difficulties.
